long_biography.plain_text:
Frank Pong Fai made competitive sailing a sustained part of Hong Kong's sporting life. He served as commodore of the Royal Hong Kong sailing club in 1989–90, chaired the local UK Sailmakers loft and advised the China Cup. His race programmes spanned Asian regattas and experimental offshore designs, joining practical sailmaking work with hands-on helming and crew development.

Pong served on Hong Kong's Hospital Authority and spent six years on the Public Service Commission. He also held roles with Hong Kong Polytechnic University and the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal. Within sailing, he arranged joint match-racing practice with China Team, using the exchange to strengthen his own crew's skills.
